chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Ya'qoob, saying: Isma'il ibn Mihran narrated to us, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated to us, from his father and Wahb ibn Hafs, from Najiya al-Qattan that he heard Abu Ja'far saying:

The caller will call out: The Mahdi is from the Family of Muhammad; So-and-so son of So-and-so (by his name and his father's name). Then Satan will call out: So-and-so and his followers are upon the truth. (Meaning a man from the Banu Umayya)

key_terms.آل مُحَمَّد: The Family of Muhammad, referring to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الْمَهْدِيّ: The Guided One, the awaited savior in Shia eschatology
key_terms.الْمُنَادِي: The caller, a figure who announces the Mahdi's appearance
key_terms.بَنِي أُمِيَّةَ: The Banu Umayya, the Umayyad clan

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the Mahdi's appearance regarding the caller and Satan?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* highlights the eschatological contest between divine truth and Satanic deception during the Mahdi's emergence, where Satan specifically aligns with the Banu Umayya to claim legitimacy. In Shia scholarship, this reflects the historical rivalry between the Ahl al-Bayt and the Umayyad caliphate, framing the Mahdi's appearance as the ultimate vindication of the Prophet's family against usurpers. The 'caller' (Manadi) represents the heavenly proclamation of the true Imam, while Satan's counter-claim signifies the persistent, albeit false, allure of political power associated with the Umayyads.
